state_production_justification.assigned_when: 2026-09-16, during the v2 freeze, BEFORE any mammalian mechanism search (states_v2.json is hashed in SHA256SUMS_v2.txt)
state_production_justification.operational_basis: REM is generated by the animal's own brainstem/hypothalamic circuitry, occurs spontaneously on a homeostatically regulated schedule, and requires no external agent or physical condition. Dedicated REM-generating populations are identifiable and manipulable.
state_production_justification.ambiguity: Ambient temperature strongly modulates REM occurrence (cold exposure suppresses it), so an external physical variable gates the state. That is gating of an endogenously produced state, not external production, so ENDOGENOUS stands. Recorded because it is the one respect in which REM resembles a physically conditioned state.
state_production_justification.note: Assignment was NOT permitted to dictate role assignments. The row's actual role profile was read off the literature; see the SLD role-scoped negative in class 7.

_species_rule_note: Frozen REPERTOIRE_v2.md section 3.3: a mechanism documented in another species never scores a cell here. This bites hard in REM, where the atonia literature is split between rat and mouse. Rat-only findings are recorded in notes and discriminating_experiment fields and score nothing. See ontology_flags_v2.

axes.units: EMG atonia (loss of anti-gravity muscle tone); phasic twitches superimposed
axes.notes: Atonia is definitional for REM scoring in mice and is directly measured by EMG. IMPORTANT QUALIFICATION: behavioural output is not uniformly reduced - anti-gravity tone is abolished while phasic twitches persist, and extraocular muscles are spared (Uchida 2021 report the atonia pathway projects to spinal and brainstem motoneurons EXCEPT those innervating extraocular muscles). 'Decreased' is correct for tone and wrong for twitches; the axis cannot hold both.

rate_amplitude.note: Cortical EEG during REM is activated/wake-like in mice; REM is scored by low-amplitude desynchronised EEG. Firing rates are not globally reduced relative to wake. Scored 'unchanged' rather than 'decreased' - a reduction claim is not supported.

coordination.note: Hippocampal theta is prominent and highly regular in REM - a state of INCREASED rhythmic coordination in that circuit, opposite in sign to what a 'reduced activity state' framing predicts.

dynamical_organization.note: Cortical desynchronisation plus hippocampal theta constitutes a distinct, highly organised dynamical regime, not a degraded one. Distinguished here from the anaesthesia rows, where organisation collapses.

axes.baseline: wake and NREM in the same animals
axes.notes: THE ROW'S CENTRAL RESULT AND THE POINT OF INCLUDING REM. Behavioural output collapses while neural activity does not fall, coordination in at least one circuit RISES, and dynamical organisation is high. v1's single-valued A_neu could not have represented this; v2 can. No sub-measure is scored 'decreased'.

NOT MEASURED IN MOUSE under the frozen species rule, and the cross-species evidence points the WRONG WAY for a suppression framing. Parmeggiani 2007 (PMID:17274181, cat and rabbit, REVIEW) reports that brain temperature RISES during REM, driven by altered cardiovascular regulation - decreased carotid and increased vertebral supply with depression of systemic and selective brain cooling. If that generalises to mouse, A_met for REM is INCREASED, not decreased. Recorded here rather than scored, because the species rule forbids transfer. THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT MISSING MAMMALIAN MEASUREMENT IDENTIFIED IN THIS STRESS TEST.

cells.ambiguity: A GAIN-of-function mutation reduces REM. The worm lethargus cell records that LOSS of the NALCN complex also reduces quiescence. Loss and gain both reducing the state is not a contradiction - Funato's mechanism is increased excitability of REM-INHIBITING neurons, so the sign depends on which cell type carries the channel - but the two cells cannot be read as the same directional claim.

mechanisms.label: NALCN sodium leak channel gain-of-function reduces REM sleep amount and episode duration

roles.basis: Reduces the TOTAL AMOUNT of REM sleep, i.e. how much of the state occurs.
Independently reduces REM EPISODE DURATION, i.e. how long the state is sustained once entered.

observed_effect.other: identified in an unbiased EEG/EMG-based screen of randomly mutagenised mice; mechanism attributed to increased excitability of REM-inhibiting neurons

perturbations.statement: A missense, gain-of-function mutation in the sodium leak channel NALCN reduces the total amount and episode duration of REMS, apparently by increasing the excitability of REMS-inhibiting neurons.

chain.step: NALCN missense gain-of-function
increased excitability of REM-inhibiting neurons
reduced REM amount and episode duration

molecules.name: Nalcn
molecules.ortholog_relation: NALCN family; C. elegans orthologues nca-1/nca-2 with accessory unc-79/unc-80 scored in S2_core_cele c1 and S5_ga_volatile_cele c1. Orthology recorded, NOT used to score.

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: increased background sodium leak conductance, raising resting excitability of the neurons carrying it

cells.discriminating_experiment: Cell-type-restricted Nalcn manipulation in REM-ON versus REM-OFF populations would resolve whether the worm and mouse results reflect the same physical operation in different circuits. Also untested: whether mouse Nalcn loss-of-function fragments sleep as the worm complex loss does.
cells.notes: ADDED BY AMENDMENT (Entry 6) DURING THE MECHANISM-OVERLAP AUDIT - a genuine miss from the first mammalian pass, found by searching the cross-state molecular question rather than the per-class question. The SAME CHANNEL FAMILY is causally implicated in worm developmental sleep, worm volatile anaesthesia and mouse REM sleep, by three independent unbiased genetic approaches, with different roles and polarities in each.

cells.ambiguity: SCOPE, AND IT IS TIGHT. The manipulation is pharmacological activation in animals whose sleep has already been PERTURBED by contextual fear conditioning; the reported effect is RENORMALISATION to that animal's own baseline, not a change from an unperturbed state. So this supports GIRK channels as sufficient to restore the state under a specific challenge, and does NOT establish that GIRK activity sets sleep in a naive animal. Graded accordingly and the restriction is carried in the perturbation record.

mechanisms.label: GIRK1/2 channel activation (ML297) restores sleep architecture after a learning challenge

roles.basis: Systemic pharmacological activation of a defined channel reverses a challenge-induced deficit in state amount and architecture. Sufficiency under challenge; not a naive-animal manipulation.

observed_effect.other: REM sleep amounts and architecture restored; post-CFC REM latency renormalised; effects confined to the first 6 h after a single-trial learning event; renormalisation to the animal's own pre-CFC baseline; associated with improved contextual fear memory consolidation

perturbations.statement: ML297, a recently developed candidate hypnotic agent targeting a new mechanism (activating GIRK1/2-subunit containing G-protein coupled inwardly rectifying potassium [GIRK] channels), alters sleep architecture in mice over the first 6 hr following a single-trial learning event. Following contextual fear conditioning (CFC), ML297 reversed post-CFC reductions in NREM sleep spindle power and REM sleep amounts and architecture, renormalizing sleep features to what was observed at baseline, prior to CFC.

chain.step: ML297 activation of GIRK1/2-containing channels
increased inwardly rectifying potassium conductance
restoration of post-CFC sleep architecture

molecules.name: GIRK1/2 (Kcnj3/Kcnj6) inwardly rectifying potassium channels
molecules.ortholog_relation: The worm volatile row's class-2 entry is slo-1 (BK), a different potassium channel family. SAME_PHYSICAL_CLASS only: both are potassium conductances promoting reduced activity, with no molecular correspondence.

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: increased potassium conductance hyperpolarising the networks that generate sleep oscillations

cells.discriminating_experiment: Kir6.2/K-ATP has been linked to cortical activity and sleep-wake homeostasis in mouse (Constantino, bioRxiv preprint, not scored: preprint and not REM-specific). A REM-specific K+ conductance test is unasked.
cells.notes: No primary peer-reviewed mouse study located for a K+ conductance mechanism specific to REM.

cells.ambiguity: PRODUCES_STATE here is scoped to the ATONIA COMPONENT of REM, not to the state as a whole. Silencing the pathway yields 'REM sleep without atonia' - the state still occurs, the behavioural quiescence does not. The role vocabulary has no way to say 'produces one component of the state'. PE-5 R2: AXIS SEPARATION. This manipulation moves A_neu (dynamical organisation: spectral power) with NO movement in A_beh or in state amount. Under the frozen three-axis rule it is a positive on one axis and a negative on the others, and it is the clearest case yet that 'affects the state' must be axis-qualified. The authors state the subunit 'does not play an important role in sleep initiation or maintenance'.

mechanisms.label: Glycinergic ventromedial medulla (GlyVMM) neurons inhibit motoneurons to produce REM atonia

roles.basis: Genetic silencing of this specific population produces REM sleep without atonia: the behavioural quiescence that defines the state's motor phenotype fails to occur.
The same paper reports GlyVMM neurons 'play an important role in maintenance of sleep', separate from their atonia function.

observed_effect.other: REM sleep WITHOUT atonia; marked decrease in cataplexy-like episodes in orexin-ataxin-3 narcoleptic mice

perturbations.statement: Silencing this circuit by specifically expressing tetanus toxin light chain (TeTNLC) resulted in REM sleep without atonia. This manipulation also caused a marked decrease in time spent in cataplexy-like episodes when applied to narcoleptic orexin-ataxin-3 mice. We also showed that GlyVMM neurons play an important role in maintenance of sleep.

chain.step: glutamatergic SLD neurons provide direct synaptic input to the GlyVMM population
glycinergic inhibition of spinal and brainstem motoneurons, sparing extraocular motoneurons
muscle atonia

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: increased chloride conductance at somatic motoneurons, hyperpolarising them and abolishing anti-gravity muscle tone

mechanisms.label: GABA-A receptor beta1 subunit shapes sleep oscillations without changing sleep amount

roles.basis: Germline knockout changes the spectral content of the state while leaving its amount and the overall sleep-wake architecture unchanged - a within-state organisation effect, not a state-generation effect.

observed_effect.other: decreased theta activity in REM sleep; overall sleep-wake architecture UNCHANGED; highest beta1 binding in hippocampus and frontal cortex

perturbations.statement: beta1-/- mice have a distinct and abnormal sleep phenotype characterized by increased delta power in non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep and decreased theta activity in rapid eye movement (REM) sleep compared to beta1+/+ mice, without any change in the overall sleep-wake architecture... the GABAA receptor beta1-subunit does not play an important role in sleep initiation or maintenance but instead regulates the power spectrum.

chain.step: Gabrb1 deletion
altered spectral power within the state

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: altered inhibitory conductance in hippocampus and frontal cortex changing network oscillation frequency content

cells.discriminating_experiment: Rat evidence independently supports this (Valencia Garcia 2018, PMID:29402935, shRNA impairment of vmM inhibitory transmission gives PS without atonia plus a ~small reduction in daily PS). Under the frozen species rule it scores nothing here. A mouse replication of the PS-quantity effect would establish whether the pathway also contributes to state amount, not only to atonia.
cells.notes: METHODOLOGICAL NOTE ON THE TOOL, IMPORTANT FOR CLASS ASSIGNMENT: the manipulation used TeTNLC, which acts by blocking vesicular release (class 5 machinery). It is a TOOL for silencing a glycinergic population, not evidence that release machinery is a REM mechanism. Class 5 is therefore NOT scored from this experiment. The proximal-effect rule assigns the mechanism to class 3.

cells.ambiguity: GluN1 deletion abolished conventionally classified REM entirely - a production-level phenotype - but the same manipulation also fragmented NREM, so the receptor is not REM-specific. Sleep HOMEOSTASIS (delta-power drive) remained intact, which the authors use to separate maintenance machinery from sleep drive.

mechanisms.label: NMDA receptors (GluN1) on GABA neurons of the lateral preoptic hypothalamus are required to generate REM sleep

roles.basis: Conditional GluN1 deletion from LPO abolished calcium signals and mice 'could not generate conventionally classified REM sleep'. Absence of the state, not a shift in its amount.

observed_effect.other: insomnia; fragmented NREM; REM not generated; effect localised to LPO (anterior hypothalamic deletion had no effect); originated from NMDA receptors on GABA neurons; delta-power sleep drive INTACT

perturbations.statement: Deleting the NMDA receptor GluN1 subunit from LPO abolished calcium signals in all cells and produced insomnia. Mice of both sexes had highly fragmented NREM sleep-wake patterns and could not generate conventionally classified REM sleep... sleep homeostasis remained intact after NMDA receptor ablation. We suggest NMDA glutamate receptor activation stabilizes firing of sleep-on neurons and that mechanisms of sleep maintenance differ from that of the sleep drive itself.

chain.step: GluN1 deletion from lateral preoptic hypothalamus
loss of excitatory drive onto LPO GABA neurons
REM not generated; NREM fragmented

molecules.name: Grin1 / GluN1 NMDA receptor subunit
molecules.ortholog_relation: Worm class-4 evidence is nmr-1/NMDA for nitrous oxide (SUGGESTED, agent-mismatched). SAME_PHYSICAL_CLASS, now with a genuine organism-level positive on the mammalian side.

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: loss of ionotropic excitatory drive onto preoptic GABAergic sleep-on neurons, destabilising their firing
mechanisms.overlap_resolution: SAME_PHYSICAL_CLASS vs worm; EXACT_MOLECULE vs S4_deep_mmus c4

cells.discriminating_experiment: Separate REM-generation from NREM-stabilisation by restricting GluN1 deletion to REM-specific LPO subpopulations, or by acute blockade timed to REM onset.
cells.notes: NEW CELL FROM PE-5 under the CORRECTED boolean protocol. The v1 concatenated battery returned zero hits for this query family. First organism-level class-4 positive in any mammalian sleep row, and it carries a PRODUCES_STATE role - rare in this table.

Deliberately NOT scored despite TeTNLC appearing in the class-3 experiment. TeTNLC is a silencing tool, not a mechanism claim about release machinery in REM. Scoring it would be the single easiest way to corrupt this row.

cells.ambiguity: Orexin B produced BOTH excitatory and inhibitory responses in distinct MCH sub-populations, so the neuromodulatory input is not uniform in sign at the cellular level even though the behavioural outcome is directional. PE-5 R2: ENTRY WITHOUT MAINTENANCE, measured in one experiment: episode NUMBER rose, episode DURATION did not. Under the frozen role axis that is PRODUCES_STATE plus CONTROLS_ENTRY with MAINTAINS_STATE tested and negative. Very few manipulations in this table separate entry from maintenance that cleanly, and it is the same separation the anaesthesia rows conspicuously lack. PE-5 R2: LIGAND AND RECEPTOR DISSOCIATE. Deleting the ligand is worse than deleting OX2R for REM but equivalent for NREM. The class-6 entry therefore cannot be summarised as 'orexin signalling'; the receptor subtype carries the NREM phenotype and something beyond it carries the REM phenotype.

mechanisms.label: Orexin receptor 2 signalling in MCH neurons gates NREM-to-REM transitions

roles.basis: The measured phenotype is the RATE OF TRANSITIONS INTO REM, not REM duration or structure once entered. That is entry control by definition.

observed_effect.other: reduced NREM-to-REM transitions; impaired insulin sensitivity and excessive feeding after fasting; female mice

perturbations.statement: Ox2R inactivation in MCH neurons reduced transitions from non-rapid eye movement (NREM) to REM sleep and impaired insulin sensitivity with excessive feeding after a fasting period in female mice.

chain.step: orexin acts on Ox2R expressed by MCH neurons
excitatory and inhibitory responses in distinct MCH sub-populations
NREM-to-REM transition rate

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: receptor-mediated change in excitability of a hypothalamic neuromodulatory population; sign differs between sub-populations

mechanisms.label: Cholinergic PPT/LDT neurons are sufficient to induce REM sleep from NREM

roles.basis: 'Activation of cholinergic neurons in the PPT or LDT during NREM sleep was sufficient to induce REM sleep.' An explicit sufficiency demonstration.
The measured effect is on episode NUMBER, i.e. on transition rate into the state, not on how long the state is held.

observed_effect.other: number of REM episodes INCREASED; REM episode DURATION UNCHANGED; obtained independently in PPT and in LDT

perturbations.statement: Selective optogenetic activation of cholinergic neurons in the PPT or LDT during non-REM (NREM) sleep increased the number of REM sleep episodes and did not change REM sleep episode duration. Activation of cholinergic neurons in the PPT or LDT during NREM sleep was sufficient to induce REM sleep.

chain.step: optogenetic activation of cholinergic mesopontine neurons
increased rate of NREM-to-REM transitions

molecules.name: ChAT-positive PPT/LDT neurons; acetylcholine
molecules.ortholog_relation: Acetylcholine also carries the two human anaesthesia class-6 entries (physostigmine reversal of sevoflurane; raised propofol induction dose), where its direction is ANTI-state. SAME_PHYSICAL_CLASS with opposite sign across states.

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: cholinergic depolarisation of REM-generating pontine circuitry raising transition probability

mechanisms.label: Orexin restrains REM intrusion through both OX2R-dependent and OX2R-independent pathways

roles.basis: Two germline genotypes dissociate the phenotype: OX2R loss gives MILD cataplexy-like REM attacks, full orexin loss gives SEVERE ones, while both give equal non-REM sleep attacks.

observed_effect.other: OX2R-/- only MILDLY affected by cataplexy-like REM attacks; orexin-/- SEVERELY affected; both equally affected by non-REM sleep attacks and disrupted wakefulness

perturbations.statement: Both OX2R(-/-) and orexin(-/-) mice are similarly affected with behaviorally abnormal attacks of non-REM sleep ("sleep attacks") and show similar degrees of disrupted wakefulness. In contrast, OX2R(-/-) mice are only mildly affected with cataplexy-like attacks of REM sleep, whereas orexin(-/-) mice are severely affected... While normal regulation of wake/non-REM sleep transitions depends critically upon OX2R activation, the profound dysregulation of REM sleep control unique to the narcolepsy-cataplexy syndrome emerges from loss of signaling through both OX2R-dependent and OX2R-independent pathways.

chain.step: orexin or OX2R deletion
loss of orexin excitation of monoaminergic and histaminergic populations
REM intrusion into wakefulness

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: loss of peptidergic excitatory tone that normally gates REM-generating circuitry

cells.discriminating_experiment: The effect was demonstrated in female mice; sex-specificity is untested. Separating the sleep phenotype from the metabolic phenotype would establish whether the REM effect is a direct circuit action or secondary to altered metabolic state.
cells.notes: Class 6 is used here for a genuinely released neuromodulator acting on a receptor - its intended sense - unlike the worm anaesthesia row where it carried intracellular transduction.

cells.ambiguity: THE SHARPEST AMBIGUITY IN THE ROW, AND IT IS REAL RATHER THAN A SCORING PROBLEM. SLD glutamatergic neurons PRODUCE atonia but are explicitly NOT NECESSARY for the REM state itself. The same class therefore carries a positive production role for one component and a negative production role for the state, from the same experiment.
cells.negative_assay_statement: Valencia Garcia 2017 (rat) knocked down vGluT2/Slc17a6 in SLD neurons and measured both paradoxical-sleep quantity and muscle tone. The assay could have detected loss of the state and did not: PS daily quantity fell only ~30% while muscle tone during PS rose dramatically with dream-enacting behaviour, leading the authors to conclude SLD glutamate neurons are 'not necessary for inducing the state itself'. SCOPE: this negative is RAT evidence and therefore scores nothing under the species rule; it is recorded because the corresponding mouse anatomy (GluSLD to GlyVMM input) is established and the negative is the strongest available constraint on class-7 interpretation.

mechanisms.label: Sublaterodorsal tegmental (SLD) and associated brainstem populations in REM control

roles.basis: SLD GABA neurons causally suppress wakefulness in mice, i.e. manipulation changes whether the animal is in a wake or sleep state.

observed_effect.other: wakefulness suppressed in both healthy and narcoleptic mice

perturbations.statement: GABA neurons in the sublaterodorsal tegmental nucleus suppress wakefulness in healthy and narcoleptic mice.

observed_effect.other: GluSLD neurons send direct synaptic input to the atonia-inducing GlyVMM population

perturbations.statement: We found these neurons receive direct synaptic input from neurons in several brain stem regions, including glutamatergic neurons in the sublaterodorsal tegmental nucleus (SLD).

chain.step: SLD population activity
descending drive to glycinergic ventromedial medulla

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: change in firing of a brainstem population that gates cortical/behavioural state and drives descending motor inhibition

cells.discriminating_experiment: Replicate the vGluT2 SLD knockdown in mouse and measure REM quantity and EMG separately. If the rat dissociation holds - atonia abolished, state largely preserved - it establishes in mouse that REM's behavioural and state components have separable generators, which is the strongest single claim available from this row.
cells.notes: Rat work (Valencia Garcia 2017 PMID:28007991, 2018 PMID:29402935) is the source of the role-scoped negative and scores nothing here by the species rule. Grenot 2024 (PMID:39121093) documents major alterations of motor control during REM in mouse models, consistent with but not substituting for the causal test.

cells.discriminating_experiment: Direct measurement of cerebral metabolic rate across REM in mouse, which would also populate the A_met axis. Currently both the cell and the axis are empty for this species.
cells.notes: No mouse study located testing a mitochondrial or metabolic mechanism of REM.

cells.ambiguity: ROLE ASSIGNMENT IS THE POINT HERE. The deletion is embryonic and the phenotype is adult, so the frozen role is BUILDS_MACHINERY alongside MAINTAINS_STATE - the animal's capacity for the state was built wrong, rather than its ongoing control being perturbed. Only two BUILDS_MACHINERY assignments existed in this table before, both in C. elegans; this is the first mammalian one, and it is carried by the ORTHOLOGUE of one of them (APTF-1).

mechanisms.label: AP-2 transcription factor Tfap2b acts embryonically in GABAergic neurons to build the machinery for normal sleep

roles.basis: The authors state Tfap2b acts during EARLY EMBRYONIC stages, and the adult phenotype follows a developmental alteration of GABAergic gene expression. Under the frozen role definitions this is construction of the machinery, not moment-to-moment control of the state.
Cell-type-restricted deletion shortens the time spent in the state and weakens its characteristic oscillation, at baseline and in rebound.

observed_effect.other: shortened REM sleep time and reduced theta power; weaker delta and theta power during REBOUND sleep after 6 h deprivation; GABAergic genes (GAD1, GAD2, Vgat) downregulated in cortex, brainstem and cerebellum but UPREGULATED in striatum; heterozygous whole-animal deletion also reduces sleep

perturbations.statement: We previously found that AP2 transcription factors control sleep in C. elegans, Drosophila, and mice. Heterozygous deletion of Tfap2b, one of the mammalian AP2 paralogs, reduces sleep in mice... In mice, Tfap2b acts during early embryonic stages... During baseline conditions, Vgat-tfap2b-/- mice exhibited both shortened NREM and REM sleep time and reduced delta and theta power. Consistently, weaker delta and theta power were observed during rebound sleep in the Vgat-tfap2b-/- mice after sleep deprivation. Taken together, the results indicate that Tfap2b in GABAergic neurons is required for normal sleep.

chain.step: Tfap2b deletion in Vgat-expressing GABAergic neurons
altered embryonic brain patterning and GABAergic gene expression
reduced GABAergic inhibitory capacity in cortex, brainstem and cerebellum
shortened sleep time and weakened sleep oscillations

molecules.name: Tfap2b (AP-2beta)
molecules.ortholog_relation: DIRECT ORTHOLOGUE of C. elegans APTF-1, which already carries this table's S2_core_cele class-9 entry as the transcriptional specifier of the RIS sleep neuron. The authors state explicitly that AP2 transcription factors control sleep in C. elegans, Drosophila AND mice.

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: developmental specification of GABAergic sleep-promoting neurons, setting the inhibitory capacity available to the adult

overlap_resolution.justification: APTF-1 and Tfap2b are orthologous AP-2 transcription factors, both assigned BUILDS_MACHINERY, both acting developmentally on the GABAergic sleep-promoting population, in species separated by ~600 Myr. This is the single deepest mechanism correspondence in the table and the only one where the ROLE is conserved along with the molecule.

cells.notes: No transcriptional/developmental mechanism of acute REM located. Timescale mismatch as in the acute anaesthesia rows.

cells.discriminating_experiment: Rat evidence is substantial and unusable here: cold exposure suppresses REM and alters its homeostasis (Amici 2008 PMID:18517040; Cerri 2005 PMID:16477956), and cerebral second-messenger changes accompany cold-induced REM inhibition (Zamboni 2004). Cat/rabbit evidence shows brain temperature RISES in REM through impaired cooling (Parmeggiani 2007 PMID:17274181). The mouse experiment - manipulate ambient or hypothalamic temperature, measure REM amount and brain temperature - is straightforward and would give class 11 its first scoreable mammalian content.
cells.notes: CLASS 11 REMAINS UNPOPULATED, AND FOR A NEW REASON. In the worm rows it was NOT_APPLICABLE (poikilotherm). Here it is genuinely APPLICABLE and genuinely untested IN MOUSE, while rich rat/cat/rabbit evidence exists that the species rule forbids importing. This is the clearest instance in the stress test where the frozen species rule, not the biology and not the ontology, is what leaves a cell empty.
No electrical-coupling mechanism of REM located in mouse.

new_evidence_added: Entire row is new; REM was not scored under v1. All evidence located in the mammalian search pass and verified through the same ledger.

ontology_flags_v2: REM DID NOT BREAK v2, AND THE PART MOST LIKELY TO BREAK IT WORKED. The axis decomposition represented the defining REM dissociation cleanly: A_beh decreased, A_neu with no sub-measure decreased and two increased. v1's single-valued axis could not have done this.

THE ROLE VOCABULARY DOES STRAIN, IN A SPECIFIC AND REPAIRABLE WAY. PRODUCES_STATE cannot express 'produces one COMPONENT of the state'. The atonia machinery produces REM's behavioural phenotype but not REM; silencing it yields 'REM sleep without atonia'. Class 3 and class 7 both carry this. A component qualifier on the role - e.g. PRODUCES_STATE(component=behavioural_quiescence) - would be the minimal repair. Flagged for the post-four-row audit, NOT repaired here.

THE SPECIES RULE IS NOW THE DOMINANT CAUSE OF EMPTY CELLS, WHICH WAS NOT TRUE IN THE WORM SET. Rat and cat evidence that is directly on-point for classes 7 and 11 and for the A_met axis scores nothing. In C. elegans the species rule was nearly free because the literature is single-species; in mammals it is expensive. This is a finding about the frozen criterion, not about REM.

Tension between the species rule (section 3.3: cross-species never scores a cell) and evidence grade E-F (defined as 'inference from another state or another SPECIES', which would yield SUGGESTED). Both are frozen and they give different answers for a cross-species finding. I applied 3.3, the more conservative, and scored nothing. This needs resolving by amendment before the mammalian grid is scaled.
A_beh cannot represent that anti-gravity tone is abolished while phasic twitches persist and extraocular motoneurons are spared. The axis is single-valued and the behavioural phenotype is not.
